subject: Telemetry & Instrumentation: Redwood POC and observability hooks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Telemetry & Instrumentation: Redwood POC and observability hooks

Hi Daniel —

Great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC: 

What we heard from Orion AI:
- Goal: embed Redwood for low-latency generation and reranking in the search pipeline; need tight observability for SLA (95th token latency target) and for model-quality regression detection.
- Requirements: header-level latency breakdown, request->response trace IDs that tie into your tracing, embedding similarity metrics, and an ability to route to a cheaper distillation model for background reranks.
- Security: procurement will want standard API-key flow initially, then evaluate mTLS for production.

Redwood proposed items (actionable):
1) SDK + auth options: provide Node/Python SDK snippets for API-key header (Authorization: Bearer <key>) and mTLS option; we'll include example env config and token rotation notes.
2) Routing & fallback: sample policy JSON for region routing + model fallback (primary: rwd-gen-7B, fallback: rwd-gen-2B-quant).
3) Structured output & tool-calling: examples for function-calling payloads and enforced JSON schema validation for downstream parsers.
4) Embeddings/reranker plan: endpoint for embeddings with cosine similarity example; suggested retrain cadence + warm cache recommendation.
5) Observability hooks: standard X-Redwood-Trace-ID header, X-Redwood-Client-Request-ID echoed back, per-request token/compute counters; we'll emit token_latency_summary and kernel_time headers. We'll also propose a Dashboard (Grafana) template with the metrics you asked for.

Attachments: Redwood telemetry checklist (PDF) and a mutual-action-plan (XLSX) with dates.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send the SDK samples and telemetry checklist (attached) by Monday.
- Priyom will put together the routing/fallback policy and a minimal infra sketch for the POC.
- Proposed POC start: week of Dec 7 — we’ll need a small test dataset and one integration engineer on your side.

Can you confirm procurement contact and whether API-key auth is okay to start? Also, are you able to share a sample request trace or the names of the HTTP header fields your tracing system uses so we can map trace IDs?

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

1) For trace correlation: we use an internal header X-Request-Trace that we propagate. Can Redwood accept a client-provided trace ID and then include an X-Redwood-Trace-ID in logs/events? We’d like a one-to-one mapping.
2) For token-level headers you mentioned — can you provide exact header names and units (ms/token, total_token_count)?
3) For the embeddings endpoint: do you expose batch embeddings and what’s the return structure for confidence/similarity metadata?

Procurement: procurement@orionai.com is the right contact. API-key to start is fine; we’ll surface mTLS as part of vendor-security review.

Lastly, we’d like the Grafana dashboard JSON export if you have a ready template we can import.

Subject: Re: Telemetry & Instrumentation: Redwood POC and observability hooks

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and attached the Grafana dashboard template link (also in the shared doc).

Trace correlation
- We accept client-provided trace IDs via X-Request-Trace (or any header you choose). Redwood will: 
  * Echo X-Request-Trace back in the response headers.
  * Inject X-Redwood-Trace-ID in logs and telemetry events; both IDs are included in our spans so you can join traces.

Token / latency headers (these will be returned on the response):
- X-Redwood-Token-Count: total_tokens
- X-Redwood-Token-Latency-Ms: total_token_latency_ms
- X-Redwood-Per-Token-Ms-P50: p50_per_token_ms
- X-Redwood-Per-Token-Ms-P95: p95_per_token_ms
- X-Redwood-Kernel-Time-Ms: time_spent_in_kernel_ms
Units are milliseconds for latency and integer counts for tokens. We can also emit these as metrics (Prometheus) and include labels for model, region, and route.

Embeddings endpoint
- Supports batch (up to 512 vectors) and returns: vector, model_id, processing_time_ms, and a confidence_score (0-1) on alignment heuristics. Sample response attached in the shared doc snippet.

Dashboard / templates
- Grafana JSON export: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-orion-telemetry (see section 3). You can import directly into Grafana; it includes panels for token latency breakdown, 95th tail by model, reranker latency, and embedding pipeline throughput.

POC scheduling
- We'll be ready to start the week of Dec 7. Deliverables for week 1: SDK sample + telemetry checklist (we’ll attach final), routing policy draft, and an initial Grafana import.

Open question for your infra team: do you prefer the trace header to be called X-Request-Trace or traceparent (W3C)? We support both; we’ll default to X-Request-Trace unless you prefer W3C.

Thanks,
Rishi
